awd_titl_txt: Conference: Conference: 2025 Biannual research and education conference of the Association of Environmental Engineering and Science Professors (AEESP) at Duke University
awd_abstract_narration:
This NSF award supports the 2025 Association of Environmental Engineering and Science Professors Research and Education bi-annual conference. The event will take place in Durham, North Carolina, May 20-22, 2025. The conference focuses on human-environmental systems under global change.  It will bring together roughly 700 environmental engineering researchers and educators to share ideas and to form new partnerships. The conference will feature workshops, technical presentations, a plenary program, and networking opportunities. The goal aims at spreading research and innovation. The event encourages participation from diverse communities.

North Carolina consortium of universities (Duke, North Carolina A&T State University, NC State, UNC-Chapel Hill, UNC-Charlotte) will host the 2025 Research and Education Conference for the Association of Environmental Engineering and Science Professors (AEESP) in Durham, North Carolina on Duke University’s campus. Approximately 700 attendees will participate in this conference. The 2025 Conference theme is “Information and Engineering for the Public Sector: Data-driven stewardship of human-environmental systems under global change”. Its program features innovations by the AEESP community in research and education to develop and translate information for the public good. The conference will strengthen the connections between the AEESP research and education community with governmental agencies and diverse stakeholders. The conference format, including Workshops, Technical Sessions, Poster Sessions, Plenary Program, External Liaison, Social and Networking, Postdoc and Graduate Networking, provides ideal means for the dissemination of research results, through close interaction of participants from industry, government laboratories, and academia.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
The 2025 AEESP Research and Education Conference was held at Duke University from May 20-22, 2025, bringing together over 1,020 registered participants from universities, research institutes, government agencies, nonprofits, and the private sector. The conference offered a vibrant program of 36 technical sessions, 14 workshops, two poster sessions, and three evening social events among other informal networking opportunities to bring together the AEESP community.

The conference theme, Information and Engineering for the Public Sector: Data-driven stewardship of human-environmental systems under global change, underscored the growing importance of data as a public good—critical for environmental protection, public health, infrastructure renewal, and sustainability. The program explored how environmental engineers and scientists can better collect, analyze, and apply information to support public decision-making in a time of increasing environmental complexity and societal uncertainty.

This theme was reflected throughout the program:

  • Technical sessions included tracks on community-driven air quality monitoring, solid waste data challenges, environmental policy translation, and machine learning in environmental applications
  • Workshops offered training on NSF proposal writing, teaching with AI, PFAS communication strategies, wastewater surveillance, and public policy engagement
  • Plenary sessions featured prominent public-sector leaders and scholars, including:
    • Elizabeth Biser (Former NC Secretary of Environmental Quality) on modernizing environmental protection through actionable data
    • Joseph DeCarolis (Former Administrator of the U.S. Energy Information Administration) on navigating the changing energy landscape with open data tools
    • H. Christopher Frey (Former EPA Assistant Administrator) on translating science for environmental policy decisions

Planning for the conference was coordinated across five academic institutions: Duke University, NC State University, UNC Chapel Hill, UNC Charlotte, and North Carolina A&T State University. Each institution was represented on the organizing committees, with shared leadership in technical programming, student activities, operations, and outreach. 

Fundung from NSF to support this event was subsrtantially leverage against several other revenue soures. 

  • Participant registration fees accounted for the majority of funding. Registration opened in early January and reached capacity by early March, with over 1,000 confirmed registrants and a substantial waitlist.
  • Sponsorship contributions totaled over $29,000, coordinated through a structured tiered system that offered visibility and tabling benefits. Sponsors included private sector companies, university research centers, and AEESP Sustaining Members. 
  • Institutional support from Duke University—provided through the Civil and Environmental Engineering Department ($50,000) and the Pratt School of Engineering ($25,000) with additional  in-kind support for facilities, staffing, and student engagement.

A post-conference evaluation was distributed to AEESP 2025 attendees using a Qualtrics survey form. The survey collected both quantitative ratings and open-ended responses across multiple areas, including technical content, logistics, accessibility, and overall satisfaction.

Approximately 18% of conference participants completed the survey. The findings provide useful insight into the experiences of attendees and their suggestions for future AEESP conferences.

Most respondents self-identified as early-career researchers or trainees:

  • Doctoral Students: 80
  • Early-Career Faculty (Assistant Professor level): 34
  • Senior Faculty (Full/Emeritus Professor): 24
  • Mid-Career Faculty (Associate Professor level): 20
  • Postdocs: 14
  • Other categories included Master’s students, government/nonprofit professionals, and undergraduates

This demographic distribution reflects the strong student and postdoc presence at the conference, which aligns with AEESP’s focus on mentorship and career development.

Overall Satisfaction

The majority of respondents expressed high satisfaction with AEESP 2025:

  • Extremely satisfied: 48%
  • Somewhat satisfied: 35%
  • Neutral or dissatisfied: ~17%

Satisfaction by Career Stage:

  • Senior and Mid-Career Faculty: Over 80% “Extremely satisfied”
  • Early-Career Faculty and Postdocs: Mixed but mostly positive
  • Doctoral Students: Largest respondent group, with strong satisfaction (29 “Extremely”).
